[P4] 出版者的话

古希腊圣哲亚里士多德曾说：‘任何人都会生气，这没什么难的，但
若要适时适所地以适当方式对适当对象恰如其分地生气，可就难上加难
了。’我们现在讲的情绪管理指的就是要适时适所地对适当对象恰如其分
地表达情绪。

现实生活中，人们越来越多地认识到情绪管理能力的重要性，因为
这方面能力出众的人往往在各个领域都游刃有余；相反，此项能力差的
人，虽然可能很聪明，但做起事来往往很吃力。

情绪管理能力虽部分得益于先天因素，但归根结底还得靠后天的学
习和培养。幼儿时期是情绪管理能力培养的黄金时期，一个人在幼儿时
期所获得的情绪经验和习惯会在大脑中形成永久的神经联结，对其身心
发展影响很长远。

当前，亲子共读情绪管理类图画书这种情绪管理能力培养方式已被
广泛认可。优质的图画书好比幸福的种子，通过父母的声音飞进孩子的
耳朵里，植根在孩子的心底，施以阳光、雨露就能生根、发芽。

这套有趣的动物图画故事书温情脉脉，每一本都是有针对性地就孩
子的某一种情绪话题展开，描绘孩子的心路历程，揭示其走出情绪困扰
并解决问题的过程。每一本书都附有幼教专家精心撰写的导读，可作为
家长亲子共读时的参考。

让我们在这套书的陪伴下，去享受一段美妙的亲子阅读之旅吧

[P5] 老师对你说
我们一起看星星吧！
一只因为搬了新家而闷闷不乐的小浣熊来啦！你看，他撅着嘴，低着头，
没精打采地拖着脚步，一脸的不快乐……
这天早上，小浣熊西蒙惊喜地发现了三朵番红花，这种花与他原来家里的花一模一样呢！也许是花儿点燃了西蒙心里尘封的喜悦，从那一刻起，他变得快乐起来了！
第二天，西蒙想去森林里探险，他很想了解这里的树木、蘑菇和居民……
一阵香气飘来，小浣熊发现了美味的黑莓，也遇到了珍贵的友谊。
如果说是番红花让西蒙重新获得了快乐，那番红花一定是大自然派来的快乐使者，大自然就是有这样一种神奇的力量。从西蒙与小狐狸相遇开始，我就不断地感慨：也许，与自然接触得越多、离得越近的生灵，就越能感受到大自然的神奇力量吧！故事中，小动物们之间的情感像极了孩子们的情感，孩子们的心灵是多么容易就能连接到一起呀，而这一点是成人可望而不可即的。我们从孩子变成大人，可孩子的境界，那种自然的状态，又是我们一生都在努力追求的。
小狐狸向西蒙介绍了其他小伙伴，原来，他们正在为第二天晚上一起去看星星做准备呢！他们要搭建一个木屋，为此还认真地做了分工，小

[P6] 责采集野果，小驯鹿负责搬运圆木棍，小松鼠负责木屋的室内装饰。而小浣熊西蒙的到来，很及时地帮他们解决了木屋搭建中遇到的困难。瞧，小动物们的世界多么有趣呀，他们互相帮助，同伴的力量是不可估量的。西蒙在森林里和这些小伙伴相遇之后，就彻底变回了原来的模样！而这也给了我们一个启示：孩子们在自发的游戏中才能全身心投入，游戏与大自然一样，拥有神奇的力量！

（保定市青年路幼儿园 张艳荣）

“啰啰唆唆……啰啰唆唆……话还真多啊！”西蒙叹了口气。

“这里才不是我的家，不是！”他抱怨道。

[P9] 确实，针叶林和西蒙曾经居住的地方完全不同：树长得不一样，花长得不一样，气味闻着也不一样，连居住在这里的小动物都不一样。

[P11] 于是，西蒙总是没精打采地拖着脚步，想念着他从前的家。
然而一天早上，他留意到，前一天夜里，地上冒出来三朵小花。

[P12] “哎呀呀，是番红花！”他嚷道，“就像我家的一样！
西蒙很开心。这让他想起自己的家，他也不那么难过了。

[P13] 第二天，小浣熊冒险向林子深处走去，想寻找其他的花。在一条路的拐弯处，
他发现几颗无比巨大的栗子，他还从来没见过这么大的栗子！
“妈妈见到会很高兴的。”他心想。

[P14] 可是还没等他去捡，“大栗子”就全都溜走躲起来了。
“栗子还能自己走呢！”看着走远了的刺猬，西蒙惊讶地感叹道。
这一下子激起了他的好奇心。

[P15] 就这样，小浣熊不再赌气了。他开始想要了解针叶林的秘密：了解这里的树木，这里的蘑菇，这里的居民……
现在，到处都可以看到他蹦蹦跳跳的身影。

[P16] 一天，空中飘来一股香香的气味。他嗅着空气，闻啊闻，顺着气味的指引，他发现一个长满黑莓的树丛。美味的黑莓！西蒙太想尝一尝了！

“我说，这都是我的黑莓！”一只正在采浆果的小狐狸说。
“又不是只有你能采！”西蒙为自己辩护。

[P18] 小浣熊低下头，很难为情。
“好吧，算了，你也摘几个吧。”小狐狸抱歉地说。

[P19] 原来，小狐狸并不坏。他还主动把蘑菇和小红莓分给西蒙吃。
“我叫奥斯卡，”他说，“我要准备些食物，因为明晚，我要和朋友们一起去野外宿营，看星星。”

[P20] 西蒙一听，眼睛放出兴奋的光芒。
“像猎人那样？”他问。
“是啊！你想不想看看我们的营地？”奥斯卡问。

[P21] 西蒙跟着新交的朋友，来到一块空地，看到一只小驯鹿满头大汗，喘着粗气，正在搬运粗大的圆木棍。
“他叫本，”奥斯卡说，“是森林里最健壮的动物。他每天刻苦坚持训练，因为他希望将来能成为圣诞老人的驯鹿。”

[P22] “来帮忙啊，别光站着聊天，”本抱怨道，“真是重死了！
奥斯卡赶紧过去帮忙，西蒙紧跟在他后面。
他也想为大家出一份力。

[P23] 本试着用圆木棍搭一个金字塔形的屋子，但只要他一放手，
圆木棍就全倒了。
“我受够了，受够了，受够了！”本生气地嚷道。
“是不是可以把这些圆木棍靠在一棵树上呢？”西蒙建议道。
他很有做工匠的天分呢！

[P24] 在小驯鹿和小狐狸的帮助下，西蒙把圆木棍分别插在一根大树枝的两侧。
虽然本有点儿不开心，但是小木屋渐渐成型了。

[P25] 接下来，小驯鹿和小狐狸采来大把大把的树叶，西蒙把树叶编在圆木棍中间。
“这样，就算是下雨也不怕啦！”他保证。西蒙一直都很喜欢搭木屋。
他很高兴能向新朋友们展示他的技能。
“真棒！”本终于心服口服了。

[P27] “注意啦！注意啦！”
只见一座长了青苔的“小山”，正摇摇晃晃地向他们移来。
“这是弗耶，他负责室内装饰。”奥斯卡解释说。

[P28] 可是弗耶的视线被挡住了，他两眼一抹黑，慢慢地往前走，一脚绊在一个大树根上，摔得趴在了地上。他手里抱着的青苔垫子，也飞到了。
“他也是森林里最笨手笨脚的松鼠。”奥斯卡补充道。

[P29] 还好，他们四个很快就把青苔垫子都捡了回来，铺在了小木屋的地
“我们今天干得不错。”本由衷地说。
26

[P30] 四个小伙伴躺在青苔地毯上，一起品尝美味的黑莓。
“当心点儿，可不能把黑莓全吃了，”奥斯卡提醒大家，
“得留点儿明天晚上吃。”

[P32] 多么美好的一天啊！时间不知不觉就过去了。
“我得回去了，现在就得走了！”西蒙说。这时，
太阳已经下山了。
“别呀！再待一会儿吧，”奥斯卡试着挽留他，“你
想不想再吃个蘑菇？”
“谢谢，但是不用了，”西蒙抱歉地说，“我妈妈
要担心了，我必须回家了。”

[P33] 奥斯卡、弗耶和本很难过，都低下了头。
他们都希望西蒙能再多待一会儿。
“你们这是怎么了？”小浣熊问道。
“你回家了，我们就再也见不到你了。”奥斯卡叹了口气说。

[P34] “但是，我家就在这片森林里呀！”西蒙不假思索地说。
“真的吗？”弗耶兴奋地尖叫道，“这样的话，明天来和我们一起，在小木屋过夜吧！你会看到，这里的星空有多璀璨！”
西蒙回到自己的家，开心极了。

[P35] 夜空中，星星一颗接一颗地亮了起来。
弗耶说得对：这里的夜晚美极了。
明天，四个小伙伴就能一起欣赏这满天的星星了。
西蒙带着微笑，在入睡之前对自己说：

[P36] “没错，从现在开始，这里就是我的家。”

[P4] Publisher's Note

The ancient Greek philosopher Aristotle once said: 'Everyone gets angry, and that's not difficult. But to get angry at the right time, in the right place, in the right way, toward the right person, and to the right degree—that's difficult indeed.' What we now call emotional management is precisely about expressing emotions appropriately, at the right time, in the right place, toward the right person, and to the right degree.

In real life, people are increasingly recognizing the importance of emotional management skills, because those who excel in this area often thrive in various fields; conversely, those who lack this skill, although possibly very intelligent, often struggle when doing things.

Emotional management skills may partly stem from innate factors, but ultimately, they rely on learning and cultivation after birth. Early childhood is the golden period for developing emotional management skills. The emotional experiences and habits acquired during early childhood form permanent neural connections in the brain, which have a long-lasting impact on physical and mental development.

Currently, the method of cultivating emotional management skills through parent-child reading of emotional management picture books is widely recognized. High-quality picture books are like seeds of happiness, flying into children's ears through parents' voices, taking root in children's hearts, and sprouting with sunlight and rain.

This series of heartwarming animal picture storybooks is designed specifically around a particular emotional theme for children, depicting their inner journey and revealing the process of overcoming emotional difficulties and solving problems. Each book includes a carefully written guide by early childhood education experts, which can serve as a reference for parents during parent-child reading.

Let us enjoy a wonderful parent-child reading journey with the company of this series.

[P5] Teacher says to you
Let's watch the stars together!
Here comes a little raccoon who is feeling grumpy and unhappy after moving to a new home! Look, he's pouting, head down, dragging his feet listlessly, looking completely miserable...
One morning, the little raccoon Simon happily discovered three red flowers. These flowers were exactly the same as the ones in his old home! Perhaps the flowers lit up the joy buried deep in Simon's heart. From that moment on, he became happy again!
The next day, Simon wanted to explore the forest. He was eager to learn about the trees, mushrooms, and residents here...
A sweet fragrance drifted by. Simon discovered delicious blackberries and also made precious friendships.
If the red flowers brought Simon back his happiness, then they must be messengers of joy sent by nature. Nature truly possesses such magical power. Since Simon met the little fox, I've kept reflecting: perhaps, the more we connect with nature and the closer we get to living creatures, the more we can feel nature's magical power! In the story, the emotions between the little animals are just like children's emotions. Children's hearts can connect so easily, something adults can only wish for. We grow from children into adults, yet the childlike state, that natural condition, is something we strive for all our lives.
The little fox introduced Simon to other friends. It turned out they were preparing to watch the stars together the next evening! They planned to build a wooden house and had carefully divided the tasks. Little

[P6] Responsible for collecting wild fruits, the little reindeer is in charge of carrying round sticks, and the little squirrel handles the interior decoration of the wooden house. The arrival of the little raccoon Simon timely helped them solve the difficulties encountered in building the house. Look, how interesting the world of little animals is! They help each other, and the power of companionship is immeasurable. After Simon met these little friends in the forest, he completely returned to his original self! The quiet night has arrived. The little squirrel Faye says: 'This night is beautiful!' I feel that this is not only Faye's inner thought, because I seem to hear Simon quietly saying the same. From this moment on, Simon has come to love his new home.

[P8] Raccoon Simon and his family moved into a house bigger than their old one, but Simon couldn't be happy.
"This is not my home, no!" he complained.

[P9] Indeed, the coniferous forest is completely different from the place where Simon used to live: the trees are different, the flowers are different, the smell is different, and even the small animals living here are different.

[P10] "You'll make new friends," Mom said.
"No way!" Simon said crossly, "This is not my home, not at all!"

[P11] So, Simon always dragged his feet, listless, missing his old home.
But one morning, he noticed that three little flowers had sprouted from the ground overnight.

[P12] "Oh my, it's crocuses!" he shouted, "just like at my house!"
Simon was happy. This reminded him of his home, and he wasn't so sad anymore.

[P13] The next day, little raccoon ventured deeper into the forest, looking for other flowers. At a bend in the path,
he discovered several enormous chestnuts—bigger than he had ever seen!
"Mom will be so happy to see these," he thought.

[P14] But before he could pick them up, the 'big chestnuts' all scurried away.

This instantly sparked his curiosity.

[P15] This way, little raccoon stopped sulking. He began to want to learn the secrets of the coniferous forest: the trees here, the mushrooms here, the residents here...
Now, you can see his hopping and jumping figure everywhere.

[P16] One day, a sweet smell floated through the air. He sniffed the air, sniffing and sniffing, following the scent, he discovered a bush full of blackberries. Delicious blackberries! Simon really wanted to taste them!

[P17] Simon had just picked a blackberry when a voice came from behind, startling him.

[P18] The little raccoon looked down, feeling embarrassed.
"Alright, forget it, you can pick a few too," the little fox said apologetically.

[P19] Turns out, the little fox isn't bad at all. He even offered to share some mushrooms and red berries with Simon.
"My name is Oscar," he said, "I'm preparing some food because tomorrow night, I'm going on a camping trip with my friends to watch the stars."

[P20] Simon's eyes lit up with excitement.
"Like hunters?" he asked.
"Yes! Would you like to see our campsite?" asked Oscar.

[P21] Simon followed his new friend to an open field, where he saw a young reindeer sweating heavily, panting, and carrying large logs.
"His name is Ben," Oscar said, "he's the strongest animal in the forest. He trains hard every day because he hopes to become Santa Claus's reindeer someday."

[P22] "Come help, don't just stand there chatting," Ben complained, "This is so heavy!"
Oscar hurried over to help, and Simon followed closely behind.
He also wanted to do his part for everyone.

[P23] Ben tried to build a pyramid-shaped house with logs, but as soon as he let go, 
the logs all fell down.
"I've had enough, had enough, had enough!" Ben shouted angrily.
"Could we lean these logs against a tree?" Simon suggested.

[P24] With the help of the young reindeer and the fox, Simon inserted the round sticks into a large branch on both sides.
Although Ben was a bit unhappy, the little wooden house was gradually taking shape.

[P25] Next, the young reindeer and the fox gathered big handfuls of leaves, and Simon wove the leaves between the round wooden sticks.
"This way, we won't be afraid even if it rains!" he assured. Simon had always loved building wooden houses.

"Great!" Ben finally admitted, convinced.

[P27] "Pay attention! Pay attention!"
A small hill covered in moss was wobbling toward them.
"This is Faye, he's in charge of interior decoration," Oscar explained.

[P28] But Faye's vision was blocked. He couldn't see a thing, walked slowly forward, tripped over a big tree root, and fell flat on the ground. The moss cushion he was holding flew away.
“He's also the clumsiest squirrel in the forest,” Oscar added.

[P29] Luckily, the four of them quickly picked up all the moss mats and laid them on the floor of the little wooden house.
"We did a good job today," Ben said sincerely.

[P30] Four little friends lie on the mossy carpet, enjoying delicious blackberries together.

"We should leave some for tomorrow evening."

[P32] What a wonderful day! Time has passed without us noticing.
"I have to go back now, I really must go!" said Simon. At this moment, the sun had already set.
"No, wait a little longer," Oscar tried to persuade him, "Do you want to eat another mushroom?"
"Thank you, but no," Simon said apologetically, "My mom will worry, I must go home."

[P33] Oscar, Faye, and Ben were sad and all lowered their heads.
They all hoped Simon could stay a little longer.
"What's wrong with you guys?" asked the little raccoon.
"If you go home, we'll never see you again," Oscar sighed.

[P34] "But my home is right in this forest!" Simon said without hesitation.
"Really?" Faye exclaimed excitedly, "Then come with us tomorrow and stay overnight in the little cabin! You'll see how brilliant the stars are here!"
Simon returned to his own home, overjoyed.

[P35] In the night sky, stars lit up one by one.
Faye was right: the nights here are beautiful.

[P1] 本页为绘本《小浣熊的新家》的封面，展示了主角小浣熊和森林中的其他动物，背景是绿色的森林，书名、作者、出版社等信息清晰可见。
[P2] 本页为绘本《小浣熊的新家》的封面，展示了书名、作者、插画师、译者及出版社信息，画面中央是戴着蓝色帽子的小浣熊从红色窗框中探出头来。
[P3] 本页为绘本《小浣熊的新家》的版权页，列出了图书的出版信息，包括作者、译者、出版社、ISBN、出版时间、定价等详细数据。
[P4] 本页为绘本的出版者序言，阐述了情绪管理的重要性，强调幼儿时期是培养情绪管理能力的关键期，并介绍了该系列图画书通过亲子共读帮助孩子认识和管理情绪的教育理念。
[P5] 本页为绘本《小浣熊的新家》的导读页，通过‘老师对你说’的栏目，介绍了主角小浣熊西蒙因搬家而闷闷不乐，后因发现番红花而重拾快乐，并在森林探险中结识朋友、准备一起看星星的故事梗概，同时穿插了对自然与儿童情感的感悟。
[P6] 本页描述了小浣熊西蒙与森林小伙伴共同搭建木屋、互相帮助的过程，以及在夜晚时分，西蒙因感受到同伴的温暖和自然的美好而真正喜欢上新家的温馨场景。
[P7] 小浣熊西蒙来到新家针叶林，一只年长的猫头鹰热情欢迎他，但西蒙觉得对方话太多，显得有些不耐烦。
[P8] 小浣熊西蒙搬进新家后感到不开心，他从树屋窗口探出头，抱怨新家不是自己的家。
[P9] 本页通过文字说明，解释了小浣熊西蒙对新家针叶林感到不适应的原因，即环境、植物、气味和动物都与他原来居住的地方不同，画面中西蒙躲在草丛里，周围是陌生的森林景象。
[P10] 小浣熊西蒙对新家感到不满，妈妈安慰他可以交到新朋友，但西蒙赌气地拒绝，坚持认为这里不是他的家。
[P11] 小浣熊西蒙因思念旧家而情绪低落，但在一天早上发现地上冒出了三朵小花，开始注意到新环境中的美好。
[P12] 小浣熊西蒙在新家的森林里发现了番红花，这让他想起了旧家，心情变得愉快起来。
[P13] 小浣熊西蒙第二天深入森林寻找更多花朵，在路边发现几颗巨大的栗子，心想妈妈会很高兴。
[P14] 小浣熊西蒙在森林里发现几颗像栗子的刺猬，它们一溜烟跑开，西蒙惊讶地感叹‘栗子还能自己走’，并因此对这些‘会走路的栗子’产生了浓厚兴趣。
[P15] 小浣熊西蒙不再赌气，开始主动探索针叶林，对这里的树木、蘑菇和居民产生兴趣，画面中他开心地在森林小径上蹦跳。
[P16] 小浣熊西蒙闻到一股香甜气味，循着气味发现了一丛黑莓，他非常想品尝。
[P17] 小浣熊西蒙在森林里摘黑莓时，被一只小狐狸发现并声称黑莓是他的，西蒙为自己辩护，两人因谁先发现黑莓而产生争执。
[P18] 小浣熊因摘黑莓与小狐狸发生争执后，小狐狸主动让步，允许小浣熊也摘几个，气氛缓和。
[P19] 小狐狸奥斯卡主动与小浣熊西蒙分享食物，并介绍自己即将和朋友们去野外宿营看星星，两人关系缓和。
[P20] 小浣熊西蒙对小狐狸奥斯卡提到的野外宿营活动表现出浓厚兴趣，奥斯卡邀请他参观营地，两人关系进一步融洽。
[P21] 小浣熊西蒙跟随新朋友小狐狸奥斯卡来到一片空地，看到一只名叫本的小驯鹿正在辛苦搬运木头，奥斯卡介绍本是森林里最健壮的动物，梦想成为圣诞老人的驯鹿。
[P22] 小驯鹿本抱怨搬运木头太重，小狐狸奥斯卡和小浣熊西蒙主动上前帮忙，西蒙也想为营地建设出一份力。
[P23] 小驯鹿本试图用圆木棍搭建屋子但屡次失败，感到沮丧；小浣熊西蒙提出将木棍靠在树上的建议，展现出他的工匠天赋。
[P24] 在小驯鹿本和小狐狸奥斯卡的帮助下，小浣熊西蒙成功将圆木棍固定在树枝上，小木屋的框架开始成型，尽管本有些不开心。
[P25] 小驯鹿和小狐狸采来树叶，小浣熊西蒙将树叶编在木棍中间，为小木屋做屋顶，他为此感到自豪，小驯鹿本也对他心服口服。
[P26] 画面展示了一片森林空地，小浣熊西蒙正在用树叶装饰他和朋友们搭建的木棍小屋，小屋靠在一棵大树旁，结构初具雏形。背景中有一只兔子躲在石头后，树上有一只小鸟，地上有蜗牛和散落的木头，整体氛围充满自然与合作的温馨感。
[P27] 小狐狸奥斯卡向朋友们介绍新成员弗耶，他背着一大团青苔，负责营地的室内装饰，画面中弗耶正摇摇晃晃地走来，背景是森林小径。
[P28] 小狐狸奥斯卡介绍的新成员弗耶在搬运青苔时因视线受阻，不慎绊倒摔在地上，青苔也飞了出去，奥斯卡评价他为森林里最笨手笨脚的松鼠。
[P29] 小动物们将散落的青苔垫子捡回并铺在小木屋内，小驯鹿本对当天的成果感到满意。
[P30] 四个小伙伴躺在铺有青苔的木屋内，一起品尝黑莓，小狐狸奥斯卡提醒大家要留一些黑莓到明天晚上吃。
[P31] 画面展示夜晚森林中，一只小浣熊坐在树桩上，面带微笑，双手张开，似乎在与前方两个动物剪影互动。背景是深蓝色的夜空和树木，地上有几朵小白花，整体氛围宁静而温馨。
[P32] 傍晚时分，小浣熊西蒙准备回家，小狐狸奥斯卡试图挽留他再待一会儿，但西蒙因担心妈妈而坚持离开。
[P33] 小狐狸奥斯卡、松鼠弗耶和小驯鹿本因小浣熊西蒙要回家而感到难过，他们希望西蒙能多待一会儿，小浣熊西蒙询问原因，奥斯卡表达了不舍之情。
[P34] 小浣熊西蒙表示家就在森林里，松鼠弗耶兴奋地邀请他第二天来小木屋过夜看星空，西蒙开心地回家了。
[P35] 夜空中星星渐次亮起，小浣熊西蒙在树屋窗口微笑，期待明天与伙伴们一起欣赏星空。
[P36] 夜晚的森林中，一轮弯月高悬，星星点点，画面中央出现一句对话：‘没错，从现在开始，这里就是我的家。’，表达了角色对新家的归属感。
[P37] 画面中，一只小狐狸背着一大捆绿色的草或苔藓，沿着森林小路行走，周围是绿色的草地、树木和野花，背景简洁明亮，充满自然气息。
